question: Flight 3851 PHX-SFO on 2026-01-03 is going to be 142 minutes late and I have spare tails at PHX. If I swap the aircraft, how many of the downstream minutes do I get back, and what does the swap not tell me?

content.text:
## What the swap buys

Baseline, holding the tail (scenario `swapB`, delay +142 on `2026-01-03|WN|3851|PHX|SFO|0855`, tail **N8633A**): five downstream legs, **+565 minutes**.

| Leg | Projected delay |
|---|---|
| `2026-01-03\|WN\|4106\|SFO\|PHX\|1055` | 127 |
| `2026-01-03\|WN\|172\|PHX\|LGB\|1440` | 117 |
| `2026-01-03\|WN\|65\|LGB\|LAS\|1545` | 112 |
| `2026-01-03\|WN\|65\|LAS\|DAL\|1735` | 107 |
| `2026-01-03\|WN\|65\|DAL\|HOU\|2255` | 102 |

Stacking a `swap_aircraft` on top of that delay clears **all 565 downstream minutes across all five legs**, plus the 142 on WN3851 itself — net **−707 system minutes**, every leg back to zero. That result is identical whichever positioned PHX tail I nominate (I ran N8963Q and N8877Q; same diff), because the model simply hands the whole remainder of N8633A's line to the replacement.

For scale against what actually happened: those five legs carried recorded `late_aircraft` of 133, 128, 124, 116 and 114 minutes — **615 minutes** of chained delay on the day, plus their own carrier minutes (1, 0, 9, 10, 25), so actual departure delays ran 144/135/140/144/155.

## What the swap does not tell you

**The cause doesn't move with the airframe.** WN3851's 141-minute arrival delay was attributed **141 NAS, 0 carrier, 0 late_aircraft**, and its inbound `2026-01-03|WN|3851|MSY|PHX|0540` landed 11 minutes *early*. Nothing about this delay is an aircraft problem — it's flow/airspace. The simulator nonetheless assumes a fresh tail departs on schedule, so −707 is an upper bound. If the restriction is on the PHX–SFO slot rather than the airframe, the swap buys close to zero on WN3851 itself and only breaks the chain to the extent the downstream legs would otherwise inherit it.

**The "spare tails" in this extract are not spare.** Every tail the tool offers as available at PHX has its own next departure: N8963Q → `WN2782 PHX-STL 08:25` (off at 15:24Z, already airborne at the 15:54Z scenario clock), N8877Q → `WN4069 PHX-DEN 07:50`, N8518R → `WN1941 PHX-TPA 07:55` (45-min turn), N8553W → `WN3134 PHX-DAL 10:25` (40-min turn). The tool's own warning says the displaced aircraft inherits the replacement's line and **that side is not re-projected** — so the 565 you recover is gross, not net. BTS carries no ground, maintenance or spare status, so I cannot confirm from this data that any PHX tail is genuinely idle; that needs your fleet status board.

**Positioning and next day.** N8633A's line ends HOU 06:05Z on 1/4 and it opens 1/4 with `2026-01-04|WN|2999|HOU|STL|0500`. Take it off WN3851 and it ends the night wherever the substitute's line ends (N8877Q finishes at SJC 06:45Z), which invalidates the following day's assumed positioning for both tails. The diff doesn't score that.

**Not in the data at all:** aircraft type (the tool explicitly does not check fleet compatibility), crew legality, passengers and misconnects, gate and station capacity. Also note the scenario clock is 15:54Z — one minute before scheduled push — so this is a decision you'd have had to make well earlier than the diff implies.

## What the swap buys

Baseline, holding the tail (scenario `swapB`, delay +142 on `2026-01-03|WN|3851|PHX|SFO|0855`, tail **N8633A**): five downstream legs, **+565 minutes**.

| Leg | Projected delay |
|---|---|
| `2026-01-03\|WN\|4106\|SFO\|PHX\|1055` | 127 |
| `2026-01-03\|WN\|172\|PHX\|LGB\|1440` | 117 |
| `2026-01-03\|WN\|65\|LGB\|LAS\|1545` | 112 |
| `2026-01-03\|WN\|65\|LAS\|DAL\|1735` | 107 |
| `2026-01-03\|WN\|65\|DAL\|HOU\|2255` | 102 |

Stacking a `swap_aircraft` on top of that delay clears **all 565 downstream minutes across all five legs**, plus the 142 on WN3851 itself — net **−707 system minutes**, every leg back to zero. That result is identical whichever positioned PHX tail I nominate (I ran N8963Q and N8877Q; same diff), because the model simply hands the whole remainder of N8633A's line to the replacement.

For scale against what actually happened: those five legs carried recorded `late_aircraft` of 133, 128, 124, 116 and 114 minutes — **615 minutes** of chained delay on the day, plus their own carrier minutes (1, 0, 9, 10, 25), so actual departure delays ran 144/135/140/144/155.

## What the swap does not tell you

**The cause doesn't move with the airframe.** WN3851's 141-minute arrival delay was attributed **141 NAS, 0 carrier, 0 late_aircraft**, and its inbound `2026-01-03|WN|3851|MSY|PHX|0540` landed 11 minutes *early*. Nothing about this delay is an aircraft problem — it's flow/airspace. The simulator nonetheless assumes a fresh tail departs on schedule, so −707 is an upper bound. If the restriction is on the PHX–SFO slot rather than the airframe, the swap buys close to zero on WN3851 itself and only breaks the chain to the extent the downstream legs would otherwise inherit it.

**The "spare tails" in this extract are not spare.** Every tail the tool offers as available at PHX has its own next departure: N8963Q → `WN2782 PHX-STL 08:25` (off at 15:24Z, already airborne at the 15:54Z scenario clock), N8877Q → `WN4069 PHX-DEN 07:50`, N8518R → `WN1941 PHX-TPA 07:55` (45-min turn), N8553W → `WN3134 PHX-DAL 10:25` (40-min turn). The tool's own warning says the displaced aircraft inherits the replacement's line and **that side is not re-projected** — so the 565 you recover is gross, not net. BTS carries no ground, maintenance or spare status, so I cannot confirm from this data that any PHX tail is genuinely idle; that needs your fleet status board.

**Positioning and next day.** N8633A's line ends HOU 06:05Z on 1/4 and it opens 1/4 with `2026-01-04|WN|2999|HOU|STL|0500`. Take it off WN3851 and it ends the night wherever the substitute's line ends (N8877Q finishes at SJC 06:45Z), which invalidates the following day's assumed positioning for both tails. The diff doesn't score that.

**Not in the data at all:** aircraft type (the tool explicitly does not check fleet compatibility), crew legality, passengers and misconnects, gate and station capacity. Also note the scenario clock is 15:54Z — one minute before scheduled push — so this is a decision you'd have had to make well earlier than the diff implies.
